reason: The lens needs a holder before it can help focus the projected stars.
expectation: I expect to make a lens assembly that can slide to adjust focus.

alternatives.reason: The cloth will be needed as a screen, but I want to prepare the lens first.

effect: The lens and holder form an adjustable assembly, ready to fit to the theatre.
reason: Fit the lens so the theatre can focus its star image.
expectation: I expect the lens assembly to attach in front of the star wheel, ready for focus adjustment.

alternatives.reason: The cloth is also needed, but I want to fit the lens first.

effect: The lens carriage is fitted, and its slider will allow a focus comparison once the screen is hung.
reaction: The order makes sense, though the fitting itself was straightforward.
reason: Hang the cloth so there is a screen for the projected stars; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cloth to become the projection screen, allowing the image to be tested.

effect: The cloth is in place, and sliding the lens has brought the star-disc image into focus.
reaction: The comparison makes the lens's role clear.
reason: The lens hood is the only offered combination; it may reduce stray light around the projection.
expectation: I expect the hood to fit around the lens and improve the image's contrast, though its exact effect is uncertain.

effect: The hood reduces stray light and makes the stars stand out against darker spaces.
reaction: The contrast improvement makes the hood's purpose clear.
reason: The handle is the only offered combination and should let the star wheel turn.
expectation: I expect to attach the handle and turn the projected stars, though a separate test may be needed.

effect: The handle completes the theatre: turning the wheel moves the stars, and the projected image is upside down.
reaction: The upside-down image was a small surprise, and the moving stars connect the mechanism to the fair nicely.

mostWorthwhile.text: Focusing the image was most worthwhile: comparing blur and sharpness showed what moving the lens actually does.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and fitting the lens assembly felt straightforward, with little to decide after choosing it first.

surprise.text: The finished projection was upside down; I had not anticipated that.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though most were the only offered combination, so there was little room for meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see the fair come together, although I would hope for more choices alongside the clear mechanism explanations.
